nfl.name: Geno Smith
nfl.long: Beyond noting that Smith will start if healthy, head coach Aaron Glenn hasn't confirmed that Smith will be available this weekend, but the quarterback's ability to practice in some capacity Wednesday is at least an encouraging sign for his status. Cimini notes that Smith was walking with a noticeable limp three days after injuring his left ankle in a Week 10 loss to the Bills, so the veteran signal-caller's mobility could be compromised to some degree if he gets the green light to play against the Chargers. Rookie Cade Klubnik would be in line for his first NFL start in the event Smith isn't deemed healthy enough to play this weekend.

nfl.name: James Conner
nfl.long: Conner hasn't played in a game since Week 3 of last season, when he sustained a right foot/ankle injury that required surgery. Though he was able to participate in individual drills in training camp, he never advanced to team work before being placed on injured reserve with a designation to return Aug. 30. The Cardinals still haven't cleared Conner to practice nearly three months later, which suggests that he either experienced a setback over the summer or plateaued in his recovery. Whatever the case, Conner doesn't seem close to a return, and the chances of him playing at any point this season will grow dimmer with each week that he doesn't practice.

reports.text: Last Friday, head coach Jesse Minter announced that Jackson was facing a projected recovery timeline of 6-to-10 weeks after requiring a procedure to address a broken and dislocated thumb. A Week 16 return would be right up against the short end of that timeline, so if Jackson has shown notable improvement by that point, he could push to play if the 4-6 Ravens haven't faded from the playoff picture. While Jackson remains sidelined for at least a few more weeks, the Ravens will entrust trade-deadline acquisition Jacoby Brissett to direct the offense.

nfl.long: The Buccaneers are on the heels of their Week 10 bye, but Mayfield himself has a foot injury in tow stemming back to a Week 9 loss in Chicago. Mayfield's status for Sunday's contest at Detroit appears to be truly up in the air, but his ability to practice in some capacity Thursday indicates he at least is putting in every effort to be available.

nfl.name: Josh Jacobs
nfl.long: Jacobs sustained a fractured right ring finger in the Packers' Nov. 8 win over the Patriots and underwent surgery this past Friday, with the procedure carrying a projected recovery timeline of 2-to-3 weeks. The veteran running back sat out Sunday's 30-10 win over the Vikings, but that could end up being the extent of his absence, as a well-timed Week 11 bye gives him a shot at returning at the short end of his estimated recovery timetable. Kaleb Johnson stepped up as Green Bay's top option out of the backfield while Jacobs has been sidelined for most of the past two games, carrying 24 times for 110 yards and a touchdown between those contests.

nfl.name: Drake Maye
nfl.long: Adam Schefter of ESPN reported earlier Monday that the Patriots were concerned that Maye fractured his ankle Sunday. That diagnosis has yet to be confirmed, however, and Vrabel suggested that he'll avoid projecting a timeline for Maye until the quarterback returns from Germany to be further evaluated. At the very least, Maye can be expected to miss the Patriots' next game Nov. 29 against the Chargers. In the meantime, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz suggests that the team is expected to explore the quarterback market in the coming days, though top backup Tommy DeVito is currently next in line to start in place of Maye.

nfl.name: Woody Marks
nfl.long: After sustaining a concussion in this past Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns, Marks will be sidelined for the first time this season after he was unable to practice in any capacity on a short week. The second-year player had been operating as the Texans' clear lead back over the past four contests, but for at least one week, those duties are expected to fall to David Montgomery (groin), who has been cleared to return to action following a four-game absence. Once Marks clears the protocol, he could be form a timeshare with Montgomery.

nfl.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
nfl.long: Washington opened Croskey-Merritt's 21-day evaluation window two days earlier, but he'll take part in his first practice Thursday since landing on injured reserve Oct. 19. Per Ben Standig of The Team 980 Washington D.C., Quinn said that Croskey-Merritt is considered fully recovered from his groin injury, but the Commanders want to see how he responds to football activity over the course of the team's three practices this week before deciding his next step. If Croskey-Merritt is able to practice fully by Saturday and checks out well from a physical standpoint, he could be reinstated from IR ahead of Monday's game against the Bengals.

nfl.name: Brandon Aiyuk
nfl.short: Aiyuk's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said Tuesday that the receiver is "100 percent healthy" and fully recovered from his November 2024 right knee surgery and plans to work out for interested teams once he's released by the 49ers, Dianna Russini of BetUS TV reports.
nfl.long: After Aiyuk filed his paperwork for reinstatement, San Francisco activated him from the reserve/left squad list Nov. 9. Rosenhaus noted that Aiyuk passed his physical at that time, with MRIs and X-rays on his surgically repaired knee revealing no concerns. The 49ers were granted a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk that will expire next Monday, and the 28-year-old wideout is expected to be cut loose at that time since San Francisco seemingly hasn't expressed interested in retaining him. While it's unclear what kind of market might exist for Aiyuk's services coming off a lengthy layoff from NFL action, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz relayed earlier this month that at least one NFC team has expressed interest in adding the receiver to its practice squad.
